ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Mumtaz Mahal

code.originalText: Prenatal visit at 27 weeks: glucose challenge, blood count, and Tdap

text.paragraph: Mumtaz Mahal returns at 27 weeks 2 days. The cystitis three weeks ago settled within two days of starting nitrofurantoin, and the culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to it; she finished the 5-day course. She has no urinary symptoms now. She feels well, with good energy, and the baby moves often. She takes aspirin and folic acid. She has no headache, visual change, swelling of the face or hands, abdominal pain, contractions, bleeding, or leaking fluid. Her family plans to travel for about six weeks, starting next week, mostly by road, and she intends to go with them. [S]

Fourteenth pregnancy at 37 (gravida 14, para 13), single live intrauterine pregnancy dated by ultrasound at 13 weeks 2 days; estimated due date July 12

Grand multiparity: thirteen previous vaginal births, no cesarean or other uterine surgery; seven living children
S — Synthetic modern problem anchored to her documented thirteen earlier births.

S — Synthetic modern problem anchored to the documented fourteen months between her last two births.
Iron deficiency anemia in pregnancy: hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, MCV 76 fL, ferritin 9 ng/mL
S — Synthetic finding; repeated pregnancies close together deplete iron. It echoes no documented diagnosis.
Acute cystitis in pregnancy at 24 weeks: dysuria and frequency, no fever or flank pain; urine culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; treated and resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent infection at an unscheduled visit; common in pregnancy and in multiparous women. It echoes no documented illness.

list.item:
Acute cystitis in pregnancy (O23.12). Resolved after nitrofurantoin. [S]
Test-of-cure urine culture sent today.

Iron deficiency anemia in pregnancy (O99.019). Hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL and ferritin 110 ng/mL: anemia corrected and iron replete after two intravenous doses. [S]
Repeat blood count at the next visit.

Fourteenth pregnancy at 37 (O09.529). One-hour glucose challenge 128 mg/dL, below 140: no gestational diabetes. Platelets 232. Blood pressure 108/68 mmHg. Fundal height 27 cm, consistent with dates. EPDS 6 with item 10 scored 0. She is RhD positive, so no anti-D is needed. [S]
Tdap given today.
Start daily fetal movement awareness from 28 weeks.
Visits every two weeks from 28 weeks; growth scan at about 32 to 34 weeks.

Grand multiparity and travel (O09.40). Travel is reasonable now if she stays well, but she must not miss third-trimester checks, and her labors have been short. [S]
Copy of her prenatal record and scan reports given.
Arrange prenatal visits where she stays, at 30 and 32 weeks, and return before 34 to 36 weeks to stay near the delivery hospital.
On long journeys: stop to walk every one to two hours, drink plenty, wear compression stockings, and wear the seat belt below the bump.
Seek care at once for headache, visual change, abdominal pain, bleeding, leaking fluid, regular contractions, reduced movements, or a painful swollen leg.
